title: Spiritual Gifts Were Never About Status
paragraphs: Spiritual Gifts Were Never About Status
You didn’t receive a gift to become impressive.
You received a gift to become useful.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Some people want the platform more than the purity.
They want the microphone more than the Master.
They want to be seen operating in power while secretly refusing surrender.
God saw it.
“You knew.”
1 Corinthians 12:7 says, “To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.”
Read that again.
For the common good.

Not for applause.
Not for superiority.
Not for spiritual flexing.

The gifts of the Spirit were never badges of rank.
They are tools of service.

Tongues without love becomes noise.
Prophecy without humility becomes danger.
Knowledge without Christ becomes pride.
1 Corinthians 13:2 says, “If I have prophetic powers… but have not love, I am nothing.”
Nothing.

Not “less anointed.”
Not “still powerful.”
Nothing.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
The real question is not, “What gift do I have?”
The real question is, “Has my heart been crucified with Christ?”
Because Satan does not fear your gift when your character is unsubmitted.

Jesus said many would say, “Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name?”
And He will say, “I never knew you; depart from Me.” — Matthew 7:22–23
That should sober us.

Spiritual gifts do not save.
Jesus saves.
Salvation is by grace through faith, not by platform, performance, or public ministry.
Ephesians 2:8–9 says, “By grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works, so that no one may boast.”

So repent of gift-idolatry.
Repent of comparison.
Repent of using God’s power to build your name.
Come back to Jesus.
The Holy Spirit gives gifts to build the body, glorify Christ, expose darkness, strengthen the weak, and call sinners home.
Not to make you famous.
Gospel Warrior, remember this:
The most gifted person in the room is not always the most surrendered.
Choose surrender.
